title: Observability intake and metric onboarding kit
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working kit for the intake, review, and onboarding of new metrics and trace spans into Redwood's observability stack. Focus is operational usability (investigation + alerting), cost control, and owner clarity.

Audience:
- Engineers adding new telemetry (instrumentation owners)
- Product and SREs proposing new SLIs/SLOs
- Dashboard authors and analytics consumers

Scope / non‑scope:
- IN SCOPE: metric definitions, minimal required metadata, tracing span naming guidance, dashboard skeletons for incident and health views, review checklist, rollout guidance.
- NOT IN SCOPE: full SLO policy, billing model changes, retention policy exceptions (those live elsewhere).

Quick intake flow (1‑pager):
1) Submit metric intake form (JIRA ticket template: JIRA-OBS-XXXX). Include raw query, owner, rough cardinality estimate, intended SLIs.
2) Observability triage (weekly triage meeting). Triage outcomes: accept, request changes, defer, reject.
3) Instrumentation PR (code change) references ticket, includes unit tests and sample dashboards.
4) Pre‑merge smoke: local/integration test that emits example points; verify in dev telemetry namespace.
5) Post‑merge rollout: staged rollout (canary) + dashboard smoke.
6) 7‑day validation: confirm expected distributions and no query cost spikes.
7) Mark metric as GA (update metric catalog).

Minimal onboarding template (copy into ticket):
- metric_name: short.kv_request.latency.p50
- owner: team/name (primary) + secondary
- contact: slack/@handle
- description: single sentence describing what the metric measures and why
- intent: monitoring | capacity | billing | product-analytics
- unit: ms | count | ratio | bytes
- cardinality estimate: low | medium | high (estimate unique tag combinations per minute)
- query (promql / clickhouse / kql snippet): exact query used to build panels/alerts
- dimensions/tags: list (tenant_id, region, model_id, route, etc)
- retention need: 7d | 30d | 90d | special (explain)
- SLI mapping: maps to one or more SLIs (include thresholds)
- alerting: yes/no + alert condition (warn/critical) + runbook link
- dashboard widgets: proposed widget titles and time ranges
- expected QPS / cost impact: rough estimate of ingest and query cost
- migration notes: existing metrics to deprecate / map from

Guidelines (do not skip):
- Prefer pre‑aggregated counters or histograms for high‑cardinality workloads. Avoid unbounded tag combinations.
- If you need per‑user or per‑request mappings, add sampling or a derived low‑cardinality rollup.
- If metric will be used for alerting, include a signal that is resilient to noise (e.g., p95/p99 + anomaly guard).
- Include a human‑readable description for every metric and every tag.

Metric naming conventions (short):
- resource.action.outcome.unit e.g., inference.request.success.count, kvcache.lookup.latency.ms
- Use lower case, dots as separators, avoid verbs in tags (use outcome tag).

Cardinality playbook (practical):
- Low (<= 100 combos/min): fine for direct alerting and dashboards.
- Medium (100–10k): aggregate by denser rollups; only surface top‑N in dashboards.
- High (>10k): require an explicit cost/retention justification and must provide a low‑cardinality rollup.

Tracing conventions (high level):
- Span names: service.operation (e.g., runtime.generate, kvcache.fetch)
- Attributes: include model.version, route, tenant_id (hashed when PII), request_type, sequence_len_bucket
- Context propagation: always propagate traceparent + baggage for tenant correlation. For private deployments, ensure no secrets or PII in baggage.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling by severity and latency. Default 5% for success paths, 100% for errors and >500ms spans.
- Long‑running / async: emit a root 'task.*' span and link child segments with explicit parent_id headers.
- Error tagging: standardized tag error=true and error_type={timeout,hallucination,oom,tracing} so queries can pivot quickly.

Dashboard design notes (practical templates):
- Incident starter dashboard (single screen):
  - Top row: SLO health (green/yellow/red badges), global token throughput, error rate p99
  - Middle: latency distribution heatmap (p50/p95/p99) split by model_family/route
  - Bottom: trace waterfall of most recent problematic request (link to trace UI) + top correlated alerts
- Service health dashboard (owner daily view):
  - 7d trend of key metrics, top dimensions by cost, paging summary (alerts fired), and a small query cost panel
- Cost-aware panels: always show ingest rate and cardinality estimates next to raw metric panels. If a panel causes >X queries/min, annotate with a caution.

Widget UX rules:
- Default time range: 1h for incident view, 7d for health view, 30m for canary metrics; allow quick toggles.
- Keep panels narrow (do not exceed 6 per row) and group related metrics visually.
- Use percentile bands (p50/p95/p99) instead of mean where latency matters.

Investigations: checklist for first 10 minutes
- Confirm SLOs impacted and scope (tenants? region?). Query SLO window & rollup.
- Check recent deploys (link to CD job) and config rollouts.
- Review traces for error_type and look for common model_id or route.
- Check top dimensions by cardinality and recent spikes.
- If high cardinality noise: flip to rollup view and evaluate one representative tenant.

Rollout guardrails (must have before GA):
- Owner declared and notified in #obs on Slack.
- Low‑cardinality rollup for any metric with estimated high cardinality.
- Cost estimate validated by telemetry infra (tag @telemetry on PR).
- Dashboard + alert smoke tests included in PR.

Decommission / rename policy:
- When renaming, create a bridging metric name that emits both old and new for 14 days and add migration note in catalog.
- Deprecation window: 30 days notice in #obs + auto‑remove after 90 days if unused.

Operational examples (realistic snippets):
- Example p95 latency alert: when increase of baseline p95 > 3 * historical MAD for >10m AND p99 > threshold -> page oncall.
- Example trace search: tag:error_type = timeout AND model.version = gptx-v1 -> aggregate top caller services.

Known questions / open decisions (TODOs):
- Do we store hashed tenant_id in traces by default? (privacy vs. investigation tradeoff) -> action: security review (SEC-734).
- Threshold for query‑cost annotation on dashboards (current proposal: 50 queries/min per panel) -> action: cost working group to confirm.
- Should we auto‑generate a low‑cardinality rollup in the ingestion pipeline for counters tagged with tenant_id? (prototype in telemetry PR)#327 -> follow up.

Next steps / action items:
- Add intake template to Confluence and link from the developer onboarding (Ava).
- Create an automated pre‑merge check that fails if new metric has >5 dynamic tags without justification (Liam).
- Schedule a 30‑minute obs office hours this quarter to walk teams through the new template (Fatima).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could try an "observability linter" that flags heavy cardinality and suggests rollups inline in PR.
- Build a small dashboard template library (json export) that engineers can import when creating the PR.
- Consider a monthly metric audit where owners confirm continued usefulness.

References and helpful links:
- Confluence: metric onboarding template (linked above)
- Slack: #obs, #telemetry, #sre-alerting
- JIRA: sample intake JIRA-OBS-4821 (example ticket)

If you read this far: please add your pain points to the ticket template -- we want the intake process to be light, not bureaucratic.

-- end of kit (working draft)
